discovery: Proposal and realization of quantum computation with trapped ions

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Rainer Blatt
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

motivation: In 1995 Cirac and Zoller showed how laser-cooled ions sharing a collective motional mode could implement a universal quantum computer, turning quantum computation from an abstract idea into a concrete physical blueprint. Their proposal founded the field of physical quantum information processing. Blatt's group then realized it with remarkable precision: the Cirac-Zoller gate, deterministic teleportation, multi-qubit entangled states, quantum error correction and digital and analog quantum simulation with strings of ions. Together these works established trapped ions as the benchmark platform for high-fidelity quantum logic. Their influence is seen in how widely the methods have been adopted in laboratories and in today's ion-trap quantum computers. Cirac and Zoller also laid the theoretical foundations for quantum networks and for quantum simulation with cold atoms. This is a clear case of simple, general theory and precise experiment together creating a new field of physics.
